fix.summary:
#131 review round 6, the final round per the owner's decision. The branch is fix/131-catalog-relative-source-is-not-cwd in /tmp/wt-131, one commit 7dc0e05d rebased onto main 00667c94. The tree is c7be2d1a, the same tree the gates and the full suite ran on as e0aa142f; only the message was amended after that. I reproduced items 1-4 on 1fcd4704 first, using the real CLI with uv 0.11.19 and pip 26.2.1 offline and a decoy in the cwd.

1. scp-style git with any user (verify B1). New extension_catalog.is_scp_git: any <user>@<host>:<path> with no :// and no whitespace is git, unless the host is spelled like a URL scheme (name@file:x stays the refused 'name @ file:x'). classify_target routes it as git, direct_reference_url excludes it, and the resolver accepts it (_is_absolute_source_url). The installer rewrites it to git+ssh://<user>@<host>/<path> as on aab1f210, now also without a .git suffix. Typed install, source add and catalog sources all work again.

2. update re-parsing a recorded path (verify B2). A catalog path is now recorded as its installer URI (_path_record_spec). update hands every path record over as a ResolvedPath (_recorded_path_target): a URI record is read back (resolved_path_from_installer_arg); an older plain-path record, from an earlier version, a typed install or source add, is re-derived (the whole string if it exists, else [extras] split off if the rest exists). _source_identity decodes URI records, so they dedupe with plain records. Typed path installs still record the plain path.

3. file:// host. The host must be empty or exactly 'localhost' in lowercase, byte-exact, for file: and git+file:, bare or after 'name @'. The refusal says to write file:///.

4. Percent-escapes. A file: or git+file: URL with any '%' in its path (before '#') is refused, and the message says to name the path directly.

5. Untrue texts fixed:
- The cwd-collision refusal now says it is aelix's own classify_target that takes a target existing on disk for a path. The refusal itself is kept.
- The extras refusal now says aelix hands paths over as file URIs and needs the project name for extras.
- The guide transcript (and its bundled copy) now shows the file URI in the installer argv.
- _url_problem names the actual problem instead of '(a URL needs a host)': a scheme a source may not use, a scheme 'name @' may not use, a relative git+file: URL, or a missing host.

6. New rows pin the dashed sdist name (review-ext-1.0.tar.gz gives review-ext, killing the split-vs-rsplit mutant), verify6 X39 (a failed refresh reached through a relative registration from another directory) and X46 (name @ git+... followed by a marker).

7. Threat model written into ADR-0255 section 12, the guide's new 'What this protects against' section (and bundled copy) and the CHANGELOG. #131 protects a trusted catalog from the current directory. A hostile catalog is outside the guarantee. Known limits are listed.

ADR-0255 also changed in its status, (B), refused items 2 and 5, the section 3 sweep rows and section 5, and gained section 13 for review round 6. The decisions README row and the docstrings are updated.

8. Rebased onto 00667c94. Conflicts:
- extension_install.py at classify_target: kept #288's code, dropped _env_truthy, kept the InstallTarget signature.
- CHANGELOG: one Security section with #131 last.
- decisions README rows: 0253, 0254, then 0255.

citations.lock.json merged with no conflict. The commit message survived the rebase (no line starts with '#') and has a 'REVIEW ROUND 6 / REBASED ONTO 00667c94' section plus an evidence section, with the exact trailer.

owner_decisions: Item 1 goes slightly beyond aab1f210, as the brief worded it: any <user>@host:path is git, including one without a .git suffix (alice@h:o/r). aab1f210 sent that form raw as pypi, where uv reads a cwd path. A host spelled like a URL scheme (name@file:x) is excluded and stays the refused 'name @ file:x' reference.

Item 2: only catalog installs (ResolvedPath) record the file:// URI. A typed path install still records its plain absolute path, so `source list` stays readable and the existing test_install_path_records_source row is unchanged. update turns every path record into the URI hand-off, older plain-path records included. If the owner wants every path record stored as a URI, it is a one-line change in _path_record_spec, but it changes what `source list` shows for typed installs.

Item 5 cwd collision: I chose 'make the message true' over 'compare only the name'. Comparing only the name would let aelix's own classify_target take a literal cwd directory 'review-ext[feature]' for a local path and install it. That is cwd substitution, which the threat model forbids. So the refusal stays and the message now names aelix's own reading.
Item 4: the percent rule also covers git+file:/// URLs, and the check stops at the first '#', so a '%' in a fragment still passes. This is listed as a known limit in ADR-0255 section 12.

blocking.title: Round-7 regression: 'aelix extension update' crashes with a traceback on a typed path record that has extras on a project with no [project] name, and skips every other extension
blocking.detail: Typed 'aelix extension install ./legacy[feature]' still works on HEAD. The directory has a pyproject.toml with only [build-system] (a setup.py-style project), uv and pip install it with featdep, and the record is '<abs>/legacy[feature]' kind path. 'aelix extension update --yes' then goes through _upgrade_source and _recorded_path_target. That gives ResolvedPath('<abs>/legacy', '[feature]'), and build_pip_args calls installer_arg(), which raises CatalogError ('cannot read its project name'). Nothing catches it: the process exits rc=1 with a Python traceback. _cmd_update's loop has no handler, so a second, healthy path record in the same settings is never updated (it does not appear in the output). On 1fcd4704 (round 6) the same update handed '<abs>/legacy[feature]' to the backend: rc 0 on uv and pip, with featdep. On aab1f210 it reinstalled without the extras, rc 0. The commit, the guide and the CHANGELOG all say update re-derives an older or typed plain-path record into the URI. That is true except here, where it crashes. Fix options: fall back to the plain string, or refuse cleanly per record, when installer_arg raises; and catch per source in the update loop. Add a row.
blocking.evidence: .omc/probes/131-live/verify7/lab7.py case legacyupdate. Outputs: legacy-head.txt (uv and pip: 'aelix_coding_agent.cli.extension_catalog.CatalogError: local path <W>/cwd/legacy is asked for the extras [feature] ...' rc=1, then 'nothing installed'). legacy-r6.txt (1fcd4704 via PYTHONPATH: update rc=0, 'typed-legacy featdep yes' on both backends). legacy-base.txt (aab1f210: rc=0). legacy_tb.py / legacy-tb-head.txt: with two records the traceback ends the run and the healthy 'other' record is never reached (grep -c other = 0).

blocking.title: The threat model (ADR-0255 section 12, the guide's 'What this protects against', the CHANGELOG) promises more than the code delivers: on the uv backend, a cloned repo's uv config in the cwd satisfies a benign package entry
blocking.detail: The text says a trusted catalog's benign entry, a package name included, is never satisfied by something in the directory aelix runs in, 'a cloned repository' named explicitly. The uv backend reads uv.toml and pyproject.toml [tool.uv] from the cwd and its parents. aelix honours that config on purpose: ADR-0200, _uv_config_files, 'explicit uv configuration is theirs to own'. Measured with the real CLI and uv 0.11.19, offline. The trusted local catalog has the entry 'local-ext'. The cwd holds pyproject.toml with [tool.uv] find-links = ["./w"] (or a uv.toml with find-links) and w/local_ext-9.9 (CWD-DECOY). 'aelix extension discover install probe --yes --index-url file://<org dir>' prints 'Install extension from pypi: local-ext' and installs '+ local-ext==9.9' with ORIGIN CWD-DECOY. That is the cloned-repo / dependency-confusion shape the owner's item 7 names. pip reads no cwd config, so it is unaffected. This predates #131 and lies outside the round-7 diff. But the newly written guarantee is false as stated, and the known-limits list does not mention it. Either list it as a known limit (uv honours a project uv.toml / [tool.uv] in the directory you run aelix in), or run uv without project config discovery, for example with --no-config plus an explicit user-level config file.
blocking.evidence: .omc/probes/131-live/verify7/uvconfig_probe.py -> uvconfig-head.txt. uv find-links and uv.toml cases: 'Resolved probe -> local-ext', argv '... uv pip install ... local-ext --index-url file://<W>/orgindex', '+ local-ext==9.9', 'installed: CWD-DECOY'. pip cases: no cwd reading (rc=1, nothing installed). grep for uv.toml / tool.uv in docs/guides/private-catalog.md and ADR-0255: no hits.

blocking.title: False refusal texts for git+file: URLs: the host and %-escape messages attribute uv behaviour that was measured not to happen
blocking.detail: _file_url_problem(url, 'git+file') reuses the file: wording. For 'git+file://h/<abs>' it says '(uv reads such a host as a directory under the current directory)'. For 'git+file://LOCALHOST/<abs>' it says '(uv reads any other spelling of the host as a directory under the current directory)'. Measured with uv 0.11.19 and pip 26.2.1 (through git 2.54): both ignore a git+file host and fetch /<abs>. uv reported the absolute repo's commit, not the cwd decoy's. A repository that exists only under <cwd>/h/... fails on both. For 'git+file:///<dir>/t%23r' the message says '(uv reads %23 as # and cuts the path there, opening another one)'. In fact uv fetched t#r correctly; pip is the one that cloned the sibling 't'. The refusals are fine as hardening; the stated reasons are untrue for git+file. Say what is true for git+file (git ignores the host; pip decodes %23), or drop the uv clause for that scheme.
blocking.evidence: .omc/probes/131-live/verify7/gitfile_measure.sh -> gitfile-measure.txt. Commits: repo c79b89f (absolute), cwd/h/... 5d278ea, cwd/LOCALHOST/... bb217f9. uv 'git+file://h<W>/repo' -> '@c79b89f...'; uv 'git+file://LOCALHOST<W>/repo' -> '@c79b89f...'; 'only-in-cwd' fails on both. uv 'git+file://<W>/t%23r' -> '@2817c05' (t#r); pip -> 'git clone ... file://<W>/t'. The messages as printed by the real CLI are in lhpct-head.txt ('git+file://LOCALHOST...' and '127.0.0.1' rows) and texts-head.txt ('git+file://h/x').
